plan: 2 Samuel 7:1-17; 1 Chronicles 17:1-15; 2 Samuel 7:18-29; 1 Chronicles 17:16-27; 2 Samuel 8:1-14; 1 Chronicles 18:1-13; Psalm 60:1-12

readings.title: YeHoVaH’s Promise to Dawiḏ
readings.subtitle: A House for the Name
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:1] And it came to be, when the sovereign dwelt in his house, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given him rest from all his enemies all around, [2] that the sovereign said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> dwells within curtains.” [3] And Nathan said to the sovereign, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you.” [4] And it came to be that night that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Nathan, saying, [5] “Go and say to <dn>My</dn> servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Would you build <dn>Me</dn> a house for <dn>Me</dn> to dwell in?</dq> [6] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have not dwelt in a house since the time that <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl up from Mitsrayim, even to this day, but have moved about in a tent and in a dwelling place.</dq> [7] <dq>“Wherever <dn>I</dn> have moved about with all the children of Yisra’ĕl, have <dn>I</dn> ever spoken a word to anyone of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>I</dn> commanded to shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Why have you not built <dn>Me</dn> a house of cedar?’ ” ’</dq> [8] “And now, say this to <dn>My</dn> servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH of hosts</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people, over Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off <dn>את</dn> all your enemies from before you, and have made you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint a place for <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and shall plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and be afraid no more, nor shall the children of unrighteousness afflict them any more, as at the first,</dq> [11] <dq>“even from the day <dn>I</dn> appointed rulers over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and have given you rest from all your enemies. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has declared to you that <dn>He</dn> would make you a house.</dq> [12] <dq>“When your days are filled and you rest with your fathers, <dn>I</dn> shall set up <dn>את</dn> your seed after you, who comes from your own body, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> his reign.</dq> [13] <dq>“He shall build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of his reign forever.</dq> [14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am to be his <dn>Father</dn>, and he is to be <dn>My</dn> son. If he does perversely, <dn>I</dn> shall reprove him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.</dq> [15] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> kindness shall not be taken away from him, as <dn>I</dn> took it from Sha’ul, whom <dn>I</dn> removed from before you.</dq> [16] <dq>“And your house and your reign are to be steadfast forever before you – your throne is established forever.” ’ ”</dq> [17] According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dawiḏ.

readings.title: The Everlasting Covenant
readings.subtitle: The Word to Nathan
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:1] And it came to be, when Dawiḏ dwelt in his house, that Dawiḏ said to Nathan the prophet, “See, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is under curtains.” [2] And Nathan said to Dawiḏ, “Do all that is in your heart, for <dn>Elohim</dn> is with you.” [3] And it came to be that night that the word of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Nathan, saying, [4] “Go and say to <dn>My</dn> servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“You do not build <dn>Me</dn> a house to dwell in.</dq> [5] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have not dwelt in a house since the time that <dn>I</dn> brought up <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, even to this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one dwelling place to another.</dq> [6] <dq>“Wherever <dn>I</dn> have moved about with all Yisra’ĕl, have <dn>I</dn> ever spoken a word to any of the rulers of Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>I</dn> commanded to shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, saying, ‘Why have you not built <dn>Me</dn> a house of cedar?’ ” ’</dq> [7] “And now, say this to <dn>My</dn> servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH of hosts</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off <dn>את</dn> all your enemies from before you, and have made you a name like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall appoint a place for <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and shall plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and be moved no more, nor shall the sons of unrighteousness oppress them any more, as at the first,</dq> [10] <dq>“even from the days that <dn>I</dn> appointed rulers over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl. And <dn>I</dn> shall humble <dn>את</dn> all your enemies. And <dn>I</dn> declare to you that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does build you a house.</dq> [11] <dq>“And it shall be, when your days are filled to go to be with your fathers, that <dn>I</dn> shall raise up <dn>את</dn> your seed after you, who is of your sons, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> his reign.</dq> [12] <dq>“He shall build <dn>Me</dn> a house, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> his throne forever.</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am to be his <dn>Father</dn>, and he is to be <dn>My</dn> son. And <dn>I</dn> do not take <dn>My</dn> kindness away from him, as <dn>I</dn> took it from him who was before you.</dq> [14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall settle him in <dn>My</dn> house and in <dn>My</dn> reign forever, and his throne is established forever.” ’ ”</dq> [15] According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dawiḏ.

readings.title: Dawiḏ’s Humble Response
readings.subtitle: Sitting Before YeHoVaH
readings.text: [2 Samuel 7:18] And Sovereign Dawiḏ went in and sat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he said, “Who am I, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>? And what is my house, that <dn>You</dn> have brought me this far? [19] “And yet this was a small matter in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>You</dn> have also spoken of <dn>Your</dn> servant’s house for a great while to come. And is this the manner of man, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>? [20] “And what more does Dawiḏ say to <dn>You</dn>? For <dn>You</dn>, <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant. [21] “Because of <dn>Your</dn> word, and according to <dn>Your</dn> own heart, <dn>You</dn> have done <dn>את</dn> all this greatness, to make <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant know it. [22] “<dn>You</dn> are great indeed, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>. For there is none like <dn>You</dn>, and there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> but <dn>You</dn>, according to all that we have heard with our ears. [23] “And who is like <dn>Your</dn> people, like Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom <dn>Elohim</dn> went to redeem for <dn>Himself</dn> as a people, to make for <dn>Himself</dn> a name, and to do for <dn>You</dn> greatness, and awesome deeds for <dn>Your</dn> land, before <dn>Your</dn> people, whom <dn>You</dn> redeemed for <dn>Yourself</dn> from Mitsrayim, from the nations and their mighty ones? [24] “And <dn>You</dn> have established for <dn>Yourself</dn> <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl as <dn>Your</dn> own people forever. And <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have become their <dn>Elohim</dn>. [25] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>, the word which <dn>You</dn> have spoken concerning <dn>Your</dn> servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as <dn>You</dn> have said. [26] “And let <dn>Your</dn> Name be magnified forever, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH of hosts</dn> is the <dn>Elohim</dn> over Yisra’ĕl.’ And let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant Dawiḏ be established before <dn>You</dn>. [27] “For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH of hosts</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, have revealed this to <dn>Your</dn> servant, saying, <dq>‘I build you a house.’</dq> Therefore <dn>Your</dn> servant has found it in his heart to pray <dn>את</dn> this prayer to <dn>You</dn>. [28] “And now, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Your</dn> words are true, and <dn>You</dn> have promised <dn>את</dn> this goodness to <dn>Your</dn> servant. [29] “And now, be pleased to bless the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant, to be before <dn>You</dn> forever. For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken it, and with <dn>Your</dn> blessing let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant be blessed forever.”

readings.title: Establishing the House
readings.subtitle: Prayer of Thanksgiving
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 17:16] And Sovereign Dawiḏ went in and sat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “Who am I, O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>? And what is my house, that <dn>You</dn> have brought me this far? [17] “And yet this was small in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>Elohim</dn>. And <dn>You</dn> have spoken of <dn>Your</dn> servant’s house for a great while to come, and have regarded me as a man of high rank, O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>! [18] “What more does Dawiḏ say to <dn>You</dn> for the esteem of <dn>Your</dn> servant? For <dn>You</dn> know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant. [19] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>Your</dn> servant’s sake, and according to <dn>Your</dn> own heart, <dn>You</dn> have done <dn>את</dn> all this greatness, to make known <dn>את</dn> all these great matters. [20] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, there is none like <dn>You</dn>, and there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> but <dn>You</dn>, according to all that we have heard with our ears. [21] “And who is like <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom <dn>Elohim</dn> went to redeem for <dn>Himself</dn> as a people, to make for <dn>Yourself</dn> a name of greatness and awesomeness, by driving out nations from before <dn>Your</dn> people, whom <dn>You</dn> redeemed from Mitsrayim? [22] “For <dn>You</dn> have appointed <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ĕl to be <dn>Your</dn> own people forever. And <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have become their <dn>Elohim</dn>. [23] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the word which <dn>You</dn> have spoken concerning <dn>Your</dn> servant and concerning his house, let it be steadfast forever, and do as <dn>You</dn> have said. [24] “And let it be steadfast, and <dn>Your</dn> Name be magnified forever, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH of hosts</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, is <dn>Elohim</dn> to Yisra’ĕl.’ And let the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant Dawiḏ be established before <dn>You</dn>. [25] “For <dn>You</dn>, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, have revealed to <dn>Your</dn> servant that <dn>You</dn> build him a house. Therefore <dn>Your</dn> servant has found it in his heart to pray before <dn>You</dn>. [26] “And now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, and have promised <dn>את</dn> this goodness to <dn>Your</dn> servant. [27] “And now, <dn>You</dn> have been pleased to bless the house of <dn>Your</dn> servant to be before <dn>You</dn> forever. For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”

readings.title: Dawiḏ’s Victories
readings.subtitle: Subduing the Nations
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:1] And it came to be after this that Dawiḏ smote <dn>את</dn> the Pelishtim and subdued them. And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> Metheg̱ Ammah out of the hand of the Pelishtim. [2] And he smote <dn>את</dn> Mo’aḇ. And measuring them with a line, he made them lie down on the ground. And he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. And the Mo’aḇites became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] And Dawiḏ smote <dn>את</dn> Haḏaḏ‛ezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah, as he went to restore his control at the River Euphrates. [4] And Dawiḏ took from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Dawiḏ hamstrung <dn>את</dn> all the chariot horses, but left of them one hundred chariot horses. [5] And when the Arameans of Dammeseq came to help Haḏaḏ‛ezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, Dawiḏ smote twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans. [6] And Dawiḏ put watch-posts in Aram of Dammeseq. And the Arameans became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ wherever he went. [7] And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold that were on the servants of Haḏaḏ‛ezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Betaḥ and from Bĕrothai, cities of Haḏaḏ‛ezer, Sovereign Dawiḏ took very much bronze. [9] And To’i sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Dawiḏ had smitten <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏaḏ‛ezer, [10] and To’i sent <dn>את</dn> Yoram his son to Sovereign Dawiḏ, to ask how he was and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏ‛ezer and smitten him – for Haḏaḏ‛ezer had been at war with To’i. And in his hand were items of silver, and items of gold, and items of bronze. [11] Sovereign Dawiḏ also set <dn>את</dn> these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, along with the silver and gold that he had set apart from all the nations which he had subdued: [12] from Aram, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Pelishtim, and from Amolĕq, and from the spoil of Haḏaḏ‛ezer son of Reḥoḇ, sovereign of Tsoḇah. [13] And Dawiḏ made a name for himself when he returned from smiting <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Arameans in the Valley of Salt. [14] And he put watch-posts in Eḏom – throughout all Eḏom he put watch-posts, and all the Eḏomites became Dawiḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ wherever he went.

readings.title: Extending the Reign
readings.subtitle: Spoils for the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:1] And after this it came to be that Dawiḏ smote <dn>את</dn> the Pelishtim and subdued them, and took <dn>את</dn> Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Pelishtim. [2] And he smote <dn>את</dn> Mo’aḇ, and the Mo’aḇites became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. [3] And Dawiḏ smote <dn>את</dn> Haḏarezer sovereign of Tsoḇah as far as Ḥamath, as he went to establish his control by the River Euphrates. [4] And Dawiḏ took from him one thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Dawiḏ hamstrung <dn>את</dn> all the chariot horses, but left of them one hundred chariot horses. [5] And when the Arameans of Dammeseq came to help Haḏarezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, Dawiḏ smote twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans. [6] And Dawiḏ put watch-posts in Aram of Dammeseq, and the Arameans became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ wherever he went. [7] And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold that were on the servants of Haḏarezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim. [8] And from Tiḇḥath and from Kun, cities of Haḏarezer, Dawiḏ took very much bronze, with which Shelomoh made <dn>את</dn> the bronze Sea, and <dn>את</dn> the columns, and <dn>את</dn> the items of bronze. [9] And To‛u sovereign of Ḥamath heard that Dawiḏ had smitten <dn>את</dn> all the army of Haḏarezer sovereign of Tsoḇah, [10] and he sent <dn>את</dn> Hadoram his son to Sovereign Dawiḏ, to ask how he was and bless him, because he had fought against Haḏarezer and smitten him – for Haḏarezer had been at war with To‛u. And he had all kinds of items of gold, and silver, and bronze. [11] Sovereign Dawiḏ also set <dn>את</dn> these apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with the silver and the gold that he had brought from all the nations: from Eḏom, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Pelishtim, and from Amolĕq. [12] And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah smote <dn>את</dn> eighteen thousand Eḏomites in the Valley of Salt. [13] And he put watch-posts in Eḏom, and all the Eḏomites became Dawiḏ’s servants. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ wherever he went.

readings.title: Help Against the Enemy
readings.subtitle: For Victory in Battle
readings.text: [Psalm 60:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have rejected us, <dn>You</dn> have broken us; <dn>You</dn> have been displeased; Oh, restore us! [2] <dn>You</dn> have made the earth tremble, <dn>You</dn> have broken it; Heal its breaches, for it has shaken. [3] <dn>You</dn> have shown <dn>Your</dn> people hard features, <dn>You</dn> have made us drink the wine of trembling. [4] <dn>You</dn> have given a banner to those fearing <dn>You</dn>, That it might be displayed because of the truth. Selah. [5] That <dn>Your</dn> beloved ones might be delivered, Save with <dn>Your</dn> right hand, and answer me. [6] <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken in <dn>His</dn> set-apartness: <dq>“<dn>I</dn> exult, <dn>I</dn> portion out Sheḵem and measure out the Valley of Sukkoth.</dq> [7] <dq>“Gil‛aḏ is <dn>Mine</dn>, and Menashsheh is <dn>Mine</dn>; And Ephrayim is the protection for <dn>My</dn> head; Yehuḏah is <dn>My</dn> lawgiver.</dq> [8] <dq>“Mo’aḇ is <dn>My</dn> washpot; Over Eḏom <dn>I</dn> cast <dn>My</dn> shoe; Philistia, shout aloud because of <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [9] Who brings me to the strong city? Who shall lead me to Eḏom? [10] Is it not <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, who rejected us? And <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not go out with our armies? [11] Give us help from the adversary, For the help of man is naught. [12] Through <dn>Elohim</dn> we shall do mightily, And <dn>He</dn> it is who treads down our adversaries.
